name: Cash-secured put writing on the S&P 500 (PUT index, the wheel)

origin.source_title: Historical Performance of Put-Writing Strategies (Cboe white paper, 2019)

how_it_works.simple: Keep cash in Treasury bills and every month sell someone the right to sell you the S&P 500 at today's price. You keep the fee; if the market falls, you have to buy at the higher price.
how_it_works.analogy: Like selling home insurance: small regular premiums, and occasionally a large claim.
how_it_works.precise: Cboe's PUT index holds Treasury bills and sells a one-month at-the-money S&P 500 put each month, fully collateralised, held to expiry. The retail 'wheel' is a single-stock version that sells puts, takes the shares if assigned, then sells covered calls on them.

rule: On each monthly expiry, hold Treasury bills equal to the strike and sell one at-the-money one-month S&P 500 put; settle at expiry; repeat.
data_needed: Cboe PUT index daily history (free CSV)
economic_rationale: Index put buyers pay above the expected payout for crash insurance. Bondarenko reports that from 1990 to 2018 the VIX averaged 19.3% while realised S&P 500 volatility averaged 15.1% (as summarised in the Cboe post).
why_it_might_fail: Losses come in crashes, when they hurt most. Single-stock wheels add stock-specific risk and assignment. The index ignores costs and taxes, and part of the history was built backwards before the index was launched.

reported_results.source: Bondarenko (2019), Historical Performance of Put-Writing Strategies, as summarised by Cboe
reported_results.notes: The PUT index rose 1835% with annualised volatility of 9.95%, against 14.93% for the S&P 500; the post says PUT had higher Sharpe, Sortino and Stutzer ratios than the S&P 500 but gives no values. Gross index values. Cboe-published, so not independent; we read the Cboe summary, not the white paper.

relevance.reason: The wheel is one of the most common retail options strategies and many bots sell it; Verify needs the index as a fair yardstick.

research.notes: Cboe publishes PUT daily history free at https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/daily_prices/PUT_History.csv; we have not added a fetcher. Added by Amanda's library batch on 2026-10-25 (options, intraday and equity anomalies that retail traders and bots claim to use).
